input.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story / scientific-educational.
Create ONE finished, gorgeous six-panel children's medical science comic page, PORTRAIT 4:5, ideally 2048 x 2560 pixels. No text anywhere: no letters, numbers, symbols masquerading as labels, logos, watermarks, speech balloons, balloon tails, balloon outlines, blank caption cards or placeholder boxes. All lettering and balloon shapes will be added separately in Illustrator. Do draw tasteful fine warm-gray panel boundaries and natural watercolor gutters. Make this a beautiful expressive storybook comic that is immediately appealing on a GitHub project homepage, not an infographic of isolated icons.

STYLE: refined pencil and ink linework with delicate watercolor washes and warm ivory paper texture; emotionally expressive, charming original human characters; warm natural lighting, subtle details, elegant composition, coral, teal, ivory and apricot palette. Science panels integrate with the story's warmth, readable authentic shapes with a little personality. Avoid plastic 3D, anime franchise outfits, uniforms on cells, factories, hard vector clipart and photorealistic gore.

Reference images are SCIENTIFIC RELATIONSHIP REFERENCES only, not style references or parts to paste. Image 1 is a general skin layer reference from NIH (hair-bearing skin; do NOT copy its hair into this fingertip). Image 2 is a wound repair sequence (show a much shallower paper cut than that diagram, and no printed labels). Image 3 is a skin immune microenvironment reference (again OMIT hair follicles, blood vessels only in dermis below epidermis); use its keratinocyte shapes. Image 4 is the NIH macrophage shape reference. Image 5 is actual platelet/fibrin microscopy: green platelet objects and red fibrin fibers are distinct; do NOT copy microscopy colors into a supposed real-tissue palette, diagrams are stylized. The activated platelets have irregular protrusions and are much smaller than red blood cells in a shared view. Fibrin is an irregular interconnected mesh, never a regular fishing net. Do not copy any labels, charts, photos, original layout, or scale bars.

PAGE COMPOSITION in normalized page coordinates (x,y from upper-left):
Top y=0.025–0.135 is a peaceful, mostly empty ivory wall / light watercolor area reserved for a two-line Chinese title at x=0.07–0.9. Tiny paper-airplane visual accent at far upper right is okay, but no major illustration behind the future title. No drawn title box.
Top story row y=0.15–0.35 has two panels: panel 1 x=0.035–0.48, panel 2 x=0.51–0.965. Main science hero panel y=0.38–0.61 spans nearly full width. Third row y=0.64–0.80 has two panels (panel 4 at left and panel 5 at right). Bottom panel 6 y=0.83–0.97 spans full width. Leave narrow organic cream gutters. No panel numbers. Preserve these areas for later lettering without drawing containers.

CHARACTER CONTINUITY: Xiaoman, an ORIGINAL 9-year-old East Asian girl with fluffy short dark-brown bob, round expressive face, coral-orange overalls over a short-sleeved ivory shirt, no logos, realistic child proportions stylized gently. Her mother has dark hair loosely tied back and a soft teal cardigan. Use the same faces and clothing each time. Neither character is a doctor or animal. No existing project character resemblance.

PANEL 1, domestic warm desk: Girl's head/body is near left-center/lower-left, her hands and partly folded teal paper airplane at lower center/right. She has just recoiled from a small paper cut on the PAD OF HER LEFT INDEX FINGER. Keep the left hand anatomically coherent (five fingers), palm-side tip visible with a tiny red spot, NOT a cut across the whole digit. Her right hand still lightly holds the plane. Her expression: surprised 'ouch', mildly disappointed, endearing, not crying. Reserve unbusy space ABOVE and to the right of her head, x=.17–.46, y=.17–.225 for 2–3 lines of dialogue. Keep fingers, face and airplane clear.

PANEL 2, same girl and mother, closer: Girl at lower-left of this panel, mother at lower-right gently supports child's LEFT hand and finishes placing a small plain bandage over the left index finger pad. The absorbent center lies over the small cut, adhesive on surrounding intact skin. This follows bleeding control and cleaning; a small clean folded gauze and soft out-of-focus sink at rear convey the setting, not a detailed instructional sequence. NO wrapping the entire hand, no red cross logo. Faces and hand contact in the lower portion. Reserve low-detail room background at x=.54–.75,y=.16–.235 for girl's 2-line dialogue and a tiny narration; another pale area x=.76–.955,y=.25–.305 for mother's two-line reply, away from her face. No pre-drawn bubbles.

PANEL 3 is the page's visual centerpiece, an imaginative but scientifically grounded view under a small bandage. LEFT half is a simple hairless fingertip SKIN CROSS SECTION, broad horizontal skin surface at approx y=.43; thin layered epidermis above a deeper soft-pink dermis. A narrow shallow cut crosses the epidermis and JUST reaches superficial dermis, where a tiny injured vessel lies. Bandage is ABOVE the skin, never inside tissue. NO blood vessels or red cells inside intact epidermis; NO hair follicles, no deep cavity, no bone, no tendon, no yellow fat. In the RIGHT half a distinct round magnified close-up of that damaged vessel-wall region shows a cluster of small irregular apricot platelets clinging together at the localized opening, mixed through with a delicate branching gold fibrin mesh. Show perhaps 5–7 activated platelets, smaller than the 2–3 softly red biconcave red cells nearby, with two tiny subtle friendly facial expressions on the foremost platelets. The mesh is an irregular three-dimensional tangle integrated through the cluster, not a rope hanging from the bandage and not a regular woven cloth. Crucially, platelets and fibrin remain visually distinct. Do not imply the entire main vessel is solidly blocked: it is a localized wall injury with patent channel nearby. Leave the magnifying connector line to later vector lettering. Reserve x=.055–.5,y=.39–.415 for a one-line narration; small unbusy margin beside skin on far left for two labels; reserve x=.60–.93,y=.395–.43 above platelet close-up for a short balloon; reserve the lower edge x=.12–.89,y=.574–.602 for two lines of explanation. Leave small clear peripheral spaces around platelet cluster for the platelet and fibrin labels. The diagram is not a wound photograph.

PANEL 4: macro close view of one pale-teal macrophage (large, soft irregular cell with a visible muted nucleus and natural pseudopod extensions). The cell is wrapping its membrane around a few tiny irregular cellular debris pieces. Draw an open membrane cup around one bit of debris plus one small internal membrane-bound vesicle containing debris, so engulfment is visible. Minimal dot eyes are okay on the cell surface but no human mouth swallowing, no hands or tools. Pink wound-tissue environment in background, calm cooperative activity. Reserve top of panel y=.647–.69 for two lines of narration, and pale low-detail space at upper-right of cell x=.25–.46,y=.70–.744 for its short speech. Main engulfment action lower-left/center remains clear. Leave small lower-right space for cell name label.

PANEL 5: return to hairless skin cross-section, same epidermis-above-dermis orientation as panel 3, more magnified at the epidermal wound edges. Show a narrow healing gap with soft new epithelial tongues extending inward from BOTH existing epidermal edges over the shallow wound bed, almost meeting centrally. Cells remain joined in a sheet, not falling as disconnected balls into the dermis. The epidermal sheet is multiple rows behind the thin migrating front, superficial keratin flattened toward the surface. Underneath, soft pale fibrous dermal tissue is still repairing. Thin neutral bandage edge can sit above skin, with no yarn entering wound. Do not show total pristine restoration, a zipper, bricks, stitches, or a deep pit. Leave y=.65–.705 in this panel low-detail for a 3-line caption and one label at the side; the main epithelium close-up fills the lower half. Do NOT generate arrows: these are added later.

PANEL 6: same girl and room, a few practice paper airplanes on the desk. Girl stands at left-center, delighted and looking after the finished teal paper airplane she has just thrown with her RIGHT hand toward upper-right. Her LEFT hand is naturally visible near waist with a tiny bandage still on the index finger, not a bandaged thumb. Lively natural throwing gesture, five fingers where visible, no extra limbs. Warm sunlight, soft teal window, curtains, charming movement. Keep major characters lower-left and airplane upper-right. Reserve upper-left corner for a small time caption, a clear space x=.35–.61,y=.845–.885 for one-line dialogue, and a naturally pale sunlit area x=.48–.94,y=.91–.955 for two-line emotional closing narration. No footer strip.

Render a finished full-page coherent watercolor comic, with the exact six scenes, strong facial acting and narrative continuity. Preserve all deliberate quiet lettering spaces. All final readable text, medical labels, arrows, balloon bodies and tails will be overlaid later; do not draw any now.
